The problem

Tokenized assets move faster than the disclosures behind them.

A token settles in seconds. The evidence that says what it is worth arrives as a document, on a schedule, and can be restated after the fact.

01

Disclosures are unstructured

Issuers publish NAV, yield and holdings as prose, tables and ad-hoc JSON. None of that shape is a rule a contract can evaluate, and no two issuers publish alike.

02

Values may be revised after publication

A figure published this morning can be restated this afternoon. A system that acts on first sight cannot tell a settled value from a provisional one.

03

Contracts cannot safely interpret prose

Solidity has no way to read a footnote. Without a machine-checkable verdict, a protocol either trusts a feed blindly or keeps real-world assets out entirely.

The Touchstone stack

Three layers, one policy record

Evidence becomes policy, policy becomes an onchain answer, and the answer is one call away from your app or your agent.

Policy Intelligence

For issuers, risk teams and data operators.

  • AI control compiler
  • Evidence monitor

Turn changing disclosures into versioned, cited, machine-checkable policy.

Onchain Enforcement

For lending protocols, vaults, marketplaces and wallets.

  • Registry v2 EIP-712
  • Policy gates
  • Guarded actions

Case study · USTB

Refused when provisional. Confirmed when earned.

A NAV value was provisional, so Touchstone refused it. The same value survived the required evidence interval, became confirmed, and changed the behaviour of a consumer contract — with no control weakened to get there.

Step 01

Provisional NAV published

The issuer posts a new NAV for USTB.

2026-08-18

Touchstone refuses

One capture cannot settle a value, so the report does not assert it.

Step 03

Value holds

The figure is unchanged across the qualifying captures that follow.

2026-08-19

CONFIRMED

NAV 11.18208300, signed and published to both registries.

Step 05

Gate flips to allowed

The same immutable contract, the same controls, a different answer.

Step 06

Guarded action executes

The permitted call lands on chain, with the refusal still on the record.

Developers

One call between your contract and the evidence

The SDK reads a policy gate over any X Layer RPC endpoint and returns the contract's own answer: allowed, plus the reason string it would give a caller. Nothing is inferred client-side.

The Solidity interface has the same shape, so a consumer contract can gate a call without an offchain hop.

Read the docs View contracts

npm install

# the SDK ships in this repository's sdk/ workspace, not on the public npm registry cd sdk && npm ci && npm run build

TypeScript

import { JsonRpcProvider } from "ethers"; import { AssetGateClient, DEPLOYMENTS, POLICIES } from "@touchstone/sdk"; // X Layer mainnet — the gate answers from the latest published report const xLayer = DEPLOYMENTS.xlayerMainnet; const provider = new JsonRpcProvider(process.env.RPC_URL, xLayer.chainId); const gate = new AssetGateClient( "0xAac48DC261B04737FDCB101D5049395121034a83", POLICIES.disclosureFreshness.registryKey, provider ); const decision = await gate.check(); // decision.reason carries the contract's own refusal string if (decision.allowed) { await admitCollateral(); }

Security and proof

Signed by a person, checkable by a stranger

Every approval decision carries the approver's EIP-712 signature, so the human step in the pipeline is itself a verifiable artifact rather than a claim about process. Reports are Ed25519-signed and offline-verifiable: download the bundle and recompute the signature, both roots and every control hash without trusting this website.
